grh_94e7b191d98e00f4c44f.title: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers
paragraphs: As a child Martha Ivers kills her domineering aunt while Walter O'Neil witnesses the crime, and their later testimony helps send an innocent man to his death. Years afterward Martha controls Iverstown and is trapped in a bitter marriage to Walter when childhood friend Sam Masterson unexpectedly returns. Martha and Walter fear Sam knows their secret, but Sam reveals he left before the killing and never witnessed it. Martha tries to draw Sam back into her life and ultimately urges him to remove Walter, but he refuses to become part of their guilt and walks away. Left together with the truth and their hatred, Martha and Walter bring their destructive marriage to a fatal end.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Lewis Milestone, [[person|gerald-mohr|Gerald Mohr]], Eleanor Audley, Jeffrey Silver, and Wilms Herbert. Other credited names include Bill Cairn as director, Richard Allen Simmons as radio adaptor, and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]].
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.95002fe4e503bf2f|The Strange Love of Martha Ivers]]. Richard Allen Simmons adapted it for radio.

grh_94716ad1bd82b78b790b.title: Chains
paragraphs: Widowed Margaret Doyle Martin has spent years giving herself entirely to her grown daughters and grandchildren, who treat her devotion as a permanent obligation. On a train trip she meets widowed mining engineer Richard Bailey, falls in love and accepts his proposal, only to have her daughters shame and pressure her into giving him up. Dr. Christian recognizes that their possessiveness has chained Margaret to a life sentence of service and bluntly tells them that being a good mother does not cancel her right to happiness. Faced with Bailey waiting for her decision, Margaret finally chooses the man she loves; they marry and begin a new life together.

The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Gloria Holden, Marian Shockley, Perry Wilson, and Berry Kroeger. Other credited names include Andre Baruch as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_9438f4c371e5947d7d0c.title: Corn Gingerbread
paragraphs: Roy Davis grows jealous when Judy spends much of her time helping visiting author Clayton Grant research a book about Rivers End. Clayton is intelligent and charming, and he eventually tells Dr. Christian that he intends to marry Judy and take her away. The surprise is that his book, Corn and Gingerbread, uses Rivers End as an example of everything he believes is wrong with small-town American life and even proposes replacing familiar local landmarks. Judy rejects both his contempt for the town and his proposal, defending the memories and human ties he cannot measure, while Roy happily reclaims his place beside her.

grh_94ae1551ff426a1ebeda.title: What to Do with Germany
paragraphs: An argumentative dramatization of Louis Nizer's What to Do with Germany frames its policy case inside a fictional 1985 America enslaved by a resurgent Germany. A father explains how the postwar Allies failed to disarm German militarism, then the program surveys earlier German leaders, nationalist doctrine, Nazi education and the weakness of relying on an imagined democratic underground. The broadcast advocates military, economic and ideological disarmament and warns that failing to reform German institutions could allow another world war and the destruction of democratic freedom.

The cast includes Julian Noa, Peter Fernandez, and Craig McDonnell. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Edward Jurist as radio adaptor, and Jack Costello as host.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.562d6d5726ce5354|What to Do with Germany]]. Louis Nizer is credited as author and Edward Jurist adapted it for radio.

paragraphs: A successful composer calling himself Adolphus Flynn becomes obsessed after hearing an older work identical to a melody he believes he has just written.
